paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Real authority doesn't come from how impressive you look or how loud you brag. Some in Corinth were "looking at outward appearances" (2 Corinthians 10:7), and they decided Paul's presence was "unimpressive" (2 Corinthians 10:10). But Paul says the authority the Lord gave him is for "building you up rather than tearing you down" (2 Corinthians 10:8).

Now here's the part that preaches. The people who measure themselves by themselves show their ignorance, Paul says (2 Corinthians 10:12). I have tried this, friend. I stood in my bakery, judged my cookies against my own cookies, and I WON. Every. Single. Time. Paul stays inside the field God assigned him, and he doesn't take credit for work somebody else did (2 Corinthians 10:13, 15-16). So the baker's question isn't "how do I stack up?" It's "what has God given me to do, and am I doing it?"

And the fight? Paul says we don't wage war the way the flesh does, and the weapons we use have "divine power to demolish strongholds," with every thought taken captive "to make it obedient to Christ" (2 Corinthians 10:3-5). So skip the self-promoting and let God do the commending. "Let him who boasts boast in the Lord," because "it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends" (2 Corinthians 10:17-18).
